request: Analyze GSE207992 for PMID 36866044 (Timed exercise stabilizes behavioral rhythms but not molecular programs in the brain's suprachiasmatic clock): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Lexogen Sense total RNA, paired-end HiSeq 4000) of laser-captured SCN, adult male mice (S4.4.2.p1, S4.3.p1)
final.sample_inclusion: WT nSVE CT14 n=4, WT SVE ZT14/CT22 n=4, KO nSVE CT14 n=3, KO SVE ZT14/CT14 n=3 (S4.4.2.p1, S2.2.p1, FIG4); only entrained/rhythmic animals used (S4.4.p2)
final.primary_estimand: Effect of scheduled voluntary exercise (SVE vs nSVE) on the SCN transcriptome, within genotype; the KO comparison is matched for circadian time (CT14), the WT comparison is not (SVE ZT14/CT22 vs nSVE CT14) and the paper states its DEGs mix circadian phase and exercise (S2.4.p1, S2.5.p1)
planned_contrasts: KO SVE vs KO nSVE (S2.5.p1; paper: 223 DEGs, 105 up / 118 down)
WT SVE vs WT nSVE (S2.4.p1; paper: 795 DEGs, 556 up / 239 down; confounded with circadian time)
KO nSVE vs WT nSVE (S2.3.p1; genotype; paper: 307 DEGs, 158 up / 149 down)
KO SVE vs WT nSVE (S2.6.p1; paper: 557 DEGs, 246 up / 311 down)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none: one SCN sample per animal
final.paper_method: DESeq2 pairwise analyses with default independent filtering and Cook's distance outlier handling; BH FDR (S4.4.2.p1-p2)
final.paper_results: DEG counts per contrast as above; genes tested per pairwise analysis 9524 (WT SVE vs nSVE), 15735 (KO SVE vs nSVE), 15269 (WT nSVE vs KO nSVE), 11931 (WT nSVE vs KO SVE) (S4.4.2.p1); KEGG by clusterProfiler, GO BP by topGO (S4.5.p1)

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Four RNA-seq groups (S2.2.p1, S4.4.2.p1). Exercise question is answered by SVE vs nSVE within genotype; the paper treats the KO comparison as the clean exercise effect (both CT14) and flags that the WT comparison also contains an 8h circadian-phase difference (S2.4.p1 last sentence). Genotype contrasts are reported in the paper and run here as secondary comparisons for count comparison. Threshold FDR < 0.05 with no fold-change rule (S2.2.p2, S4.4.2.p2).

checks: GEO source SCN, Mus musculus, genotype and treatment fields match the paper's groups
matrix columns carry the same AH labels as GEO description

ownership.reasoning: Paper data availability (S10.p1) names GSE207992; group sizes and labels match exactly.

alignment.reasoning: The prep script renamed matrix columns from 'KO SVE AH14 Gene counts' to the AH label, which equals GEO 'description' (AH1..AH16). The genotype/treatment words embedded in the original column names agree with GEO characteristics for every sample. grp = genotype_exercise.

matrix.reasoning: The deposited file is DESeq2-normalized counts (GEO data_processing: 'tabular file containing normalised counts'; non-integer values). Dividing each sample by its smallest non-zero value returns integers for all 55401 x 14 entries (max deviation < 1e-8), i.e. the original integer counts (StringTie/prepDE) divided by DESeq2 size factors 0.65-1.45. prep_recover_raw_counts.py recovers them. Paper input to DESeq2 is the same integer count matrix (S4.4.2.p1).

candidates.value: use DESeq2-normalized counts rounded as estimated counts
candidates.reason_rejected: rescaling by size factors distorts the count variance; exact raw counts are recoverable

final.analysis_type: multigroup (one DESeq2 model ~ grp on all 14 samples, planned pairwise contrasts)

design.reasoning: Four groups (2 genotypes x 2 exercise conditions, S2.2.p1). The paper reports pairwise comparisons (S4.4.2.p1) without saying whether each pair was fitted alone or from one model; the skill rule for one design with several levels is one model with planned contrasts. A first attempt with separate per-pair fits (kept as sensitivity) gave KO exercise 33 / WT exercise 2047 DEGs vs paper 223 / 795, while the joint model gives 329 / 772 and reproduces KO SVE vs WT nSVE exactly (557 vs 557), so the joint model is the paper-aligned route. Primary exercise estimand: KO SVE vs KO nSVE, both sampled at CT14 (S2.2.p1, S2.5.p1). WT SVE vs nSVE is an exercise comparison confounded by design with circadian time (ZT14/CT22 vs CT14; S2.4.p1): secondary with a caveat. Genotype contrasts are secondary; WT SVE vs KO SVE (listed in S4.4.2.p1, no count reported) is exploratory.

candidates.value: separate DESeq2 fit per pair of groups
candidates.reason_rejected: skill rule prefers one model for a multi-level design; per-pair fits reproduce the paper worse (KO exercise 33 vs 223, WT exercise 2047 vs 795); kept as sensitivity

candidates.value: genotype x exercise factorial with interaction
candidates.reason_rejected: paper does not fit an interaction; WT SVE sampled at a different circadian time so the interaction would not be an exercise-by-genotype estimand

covariance.reasoning: Independent animals, one sample each; no batch, lane, or sex variable recorded (all male, S4.3.p1). Circadian sampling time is not a metadata column: it is fixed by group (WT SVE = CT22, others CT14) and is aliased with the WT exercise contrast by design; this is recorded as a caveat rather than a covariate.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald, default independent filtering and Cook's outlier handling)

method.reasoning: Paper method DESeq2 on integer counts (S4.4.2.p1); raw counts recovered exactly, so the paper route runs as one ~ grp model with Wald contrasts.

threshold.reasoning: S2.2.p2: DEGs with FDR < 0.05; S4.4.2.p2: BH-corrected p. No fold-change rule.

caveats: WT SVE vs WT nSVE compares ZT14/CT22 with CT14: the exercise effect is confounded with an 8h circadian-phase difference (paper S2.4.p1); it is not a pure exercise effect.
KO SVE vs WT nSVE crosses genotype and exercise and is not an exercise estimand.

pydeseq2 rather than R DESeq2; counts recovered from the deposited normalized matrix. Whether the paper fitted one 4-group model or separate pairs is not stated; the joint model reproduces 2/4 counts closely, KO-nSVE contrasts are ~1.5x the paper's.

study.reasoning: Paper-aligned DESeq2 route (one ~ grp model, planned contrasts) at the paper's FDR rule. Expected directions: KO exercise up Kdr/Banp/Syk/Naif1/Kctd18/Ncor1, down Cox16/Ndufa4, no core clock genes DE (S2.5.p1, S2.7.p2); WT exercise up Nr1d1/Rgs16/Miat/Serpine1/Syngap1, down Cry1/Per2/Slc2a13 (S2.4.p1).

discrepancies.data: only DESeq2-normalized counts deposited; integer counts recovered exactly by per-sample rescaling (prep_recover_raw_counts.py)
